claims: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down at 5:07 p.m. PDT on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II crew was recovered by the USS John P. Murtha.
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
The Artemis II mission concluded the first human flyby of the Moon in over 50 years.
The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft performed a successful reentry.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft performed a parachute-assisted splashdown.
The splashdown marked the official end of the Artemis II crewed mission
